description: Establish the green baseline and produce the required second-pass deep-audit report as a checked-in artifact. This is analysis + documentation only; NO source code changes in this feature. Confirm the baseline is green, then write the full structured audit report covering all 10 audit domains (security incl. XSS/DOM-XSS/eval/injection/SSRF; Electron security incl. IPC/contextBridge/nav guards/webPreferences; dependencies incl. npm audit + electron/extract-zip CVE status; error handling; resource leaks; Steam/GC/protobuf validation; testing; architecture; performance; code quality) grounded in the actual code. The report MUST use exactly the 9 required sections in order: 1. CRITICAL, 2. HIGH, 3. MEDIUM, 4. LOW, 5. FALSE POSITIVE (leave, with reason), 6. DEPENDENCY RISKS, 7. SECURITY RISKS, 8. TEST COVERAGE, 9. REGRESSION RISKS. This feature is independent of FEAT-002 in terms of file edits, but should be completed first so the fixes in FEAT-002 are justified by the report.
steps: Confirm baseline green by running: `npm test` (expect 133 pass / 0 fail), `npm run lint` (expect clean), `npm audit` (expect 0 vulnerabilities), `npm run package` (expect dist/linux-unpacked built; Windows wine failure is expected and NOT a regression). Record the exact numbers.

Re-read the primary DOM-XSS finding in context.json (primary_finding) and confirm it against html/js/front.js '.show-maps' handler and helpers/gcpd_parser.js extractCompetitiveMaps/parseCompetitiveMapRow. Trace how mapName and skill_group flow from scraped GCPD HTML into row.innerHTML text nodes and alt/title attributes without escaping.

Audit the rest of the security surface and CONFIRM the already-safe items so they can be listed as FALSE POSITIVE with reasons: changelog innerHTML via markdown-it html:false (safe); account name/level/ban cells use innerText (safe); no eval/new Function/string-setTimeout anywhere (verify with grep); protoDecode/protoEncode defensive; shell.openExternal restricted to http/https via nav guards; will-navigate + setWindowOpenHandler deny on all windows; EncryptedStorage AES-256-GCM authenticated with never-write-on-decrypt-error.

Audit Electron posture: webPreferences (contextIsolation:true, sandbox:false intentional, no nodeIntegration), contextBridge surface in preload.js (ipcRenderer send/on/invoke variadic, fastEqual, friendCode, clipboard.writeText guarded, shell.openExternal, md_converter). Assess whether any IPC handler in main.js trusts renderer input unsafely (accounts:add/update/delete, settings:set, steamtotp, steam:steamguard:response) and whether nav guards cover main + all prompt windows (they do via wirePromptWindowCommon).

Audit dependencies: run `npm audit`, confirm 0 vulnerabilities. Document that the historical electron/extract-zip advisories are resolved by electron ^44.1.0 (report the CVE lineage at a high level and that no vulnerable version is currently resolved). Note overrides for steam-appticket and adm-zip. Do NOT bump anything.

Audit error handling (empty/error-hiding catches vs intentionally-documented safe-to-ignore catches), resource leaks (gcHelloInterval, outerTimeout, gcTimeout, steamGuard ipcMain listener teardown across every terminal path in check_account, update_cycle setTimeout in front.js), Steam/GC/protobuf null/undefined/type/enum/corrupt handling, performance (500ms updateAccounts polling loop, per-map innerHTML rebuild), and code quality (Russian-comment debug console.log in renderRowPrime, magic numbers). Distinguish real issues from intentional design.

Write the report to .agents/tasks/task-deep-audit-2/AUDIT-REPORT.md using EXACTLY these 9 top-level sections in order: '1. CRITICAL', '2. HIGH', '3. MEDIUM', '4. LOW', '5. FALSE POSITIVE', '6. DEPENDENCY RISKS', '7. SECURITY RISKS', '8. TEST COVERAGE', '9. REGRESSION RISKS'. Place the maps-modal attribute-injection DOM-XSS under CRITICAL or HIGH with precise file/line references and the exact exploit shape. For each real fixable issue, note the intended fix and whether a regression test is feasible. List the confirmed-safe items under FALSE POSITIVE with the reason each is safe.
Record the baseline verification numbers in the FEAT-001 findings field.
acceptance_criteria: `.agents/tasks/task-deep-audit-2/AUDIT-REPORT.md` exists and contains all 9 required sections in the exact order and naming specified.

The DOM-XSS maps-modal attribute-injection finding is documented with the concrete file (html/js/front.js), the sink (row.innerHTML in the '.show-maps' handler), the source (helpers/gcpd_parser.js extractCompetitiveMaps scraped mapName/skill_group), and the exploit shape (attribute breakout via a `"` since [^<] does not block quotes).

The report explicitly lists the already-safe items (changelog markdown-it html:false, innerText usages, no eval, defensive protoDecode, nav guards, AES-GCM) under FALSE POSITIVE with reasons, so they are not 'fixed' pointlessly.
No source files under html/, helpers/, main.js, preload.js, or EncryptedStorage.js are modified in this feature (report only).
Running `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm audit` still green after this feature (they should be unchanged since no code was touched).
verification: Run `npm test` and confirm 133 pass / 0 fail.
Run `npm run lint` and confirm clean.
Confirm .agents/tasks/task-deep-audit-2/AUDIT-REPORT.md exists with the 9 required sections (read the file).
Confirm `git status` shows no modifications to source files (only the new report + task artifacts).
findings: Baseline verified GREEN before writing report: `npm test` = 133 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped; `npm run lint` (eslint .) = clean; `npm audit` = found 0 vulnerabilities; `npm run package` (electron-builder --dir) = dist/linux-unpacked built on electron 44.1.0 (Windows target fails only for missing wine, EXPECTED, not a regression). AUDIT-REPORT.md written with all 9 required sections in order. Primary DOM-XSS confirmed in code: sink html/js/front.js '.show-maps' handler row.innerHTML (~L1031-1050) interpolates scraped mapName + mapData.skill_group into alt/title attributes with no escaping; source helpers/gcpd_parser.js extractCompetitiveMaps/parseCompetitiveMapRow (~L505-560) regex [^<] blocks '<' but not '"', enabling attribute breakout (x" onerror="...). Documented as CRITICAL (C-1) due to preload IPC reach. Secondary showToast .innerHTML (front.js L43) with ret.error at L629/795/810 documented as HIGH (H-1). Confirmed-safe items listed under FALSE POSITIVE: changelog markdown-it html:false, innerText cells, no eval/new Function/string-timers (repo-wide grep = 0 matches), defensive protoDecode/protoEncode, nav guards on all windows via wirePromptWindowCommon, AES-256-GCM. Dependencies: npm audit 0 vulns; electron@44.1.0 resolves historic advisories; extract-zip NOT in tree (npm ls = empty); overrides steam-appticket ^2.0.1 + adm-zip ^0.6.0 intentional. NOTE: front.js DOES have a 500ms self-rescheduling polling loop at L662 (update_cycle = setTimeout(updateAccounts, 500)) despite event-driven accounts:updated - documented as MEDIUM M-3. No source files modified in this feature (git status shows only .agents/ artifacts + AUDIT-REPORT.md).
